title: Price a contract in the years it is paid

blocks.text: A gas distribution company (invented for this practice) prices main replacement from a price book compiled in `price_year`. A job's estimate is a tuple of yearly amounts in $k, one per year of work, all at price-book prices. The contractor bills each year's work at the prices of the year it is done, and the contract says prices rise by `escalation` a year.
Write `billed(estimate, price_year, start, escalation)`, returning `{calendar year: amount billed}` for a job that starts in `start`. The job may start in the price-book year or later.
Write the formula for the amount billed in calendar year $`y`$ first, and say what its exponent counts from. About four lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from contract import billed

estimate = (600, 300, 150)

print("priced 2025, start 2025, 3%:", {y: round(v, 2) for y, v in billed(estimate, 2025, 2025, 0.03).items()})
print("priced 2025, start 2028, 3%:", {y: round(v, 2) for y, v in billed(estimate, 2025, 2028, 0.03).items()})
print("priced 2025, start 2028, 0%:", {y: round(v, 2) for y, v in billed(estimate, 2025, 2028, 0.0).items()})

cases.says: with no escalation, the k-th year of work is billed in calendar year start + k at its quoted amount
work starting after the price-book year is escalated for every year since the price book, not since the start
an amount billed in the price-book year itself is not escalated
